title: CRISPR-based manipulation and visualization of endogenous α-synuclein in mouse neurons
author: Parra-Rivas, Sharma, et al.
materials: N-PER Neuronal Protein Extraction Reagent (Thermo Scientific, Cat# 87792)
100X Protease and Phosphatase Inhibitor Cocktail (Cell Signaling, Cat# 5872)

steps.title: Prepare NB/B27 culture medium
steps.instruction: Make neuronal culture medium (NB/B27) by adding 10 mL B27 supplement (Gibco, Cat# 17504044) to 500 mL Neurobasal (Gibco, Cat# 21103049), then add 5 mL penicillin‑streptomycin (Gibco, Cat# 15140122) and 5 mL GlutaMAX (Thermo Fisher, Cat# 35050061). Invert gently to mix, filter‑sterilize through a 0.22 µm filter, store at 4 °C (up to 1 month) and warm to 37 °C before use. Final concentrations are 1× B27, 1× pen‑strep, 1× GlutaMAX.

steps.title: Prepare neuronal lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Combine N‑PER Neuronal Protein Extraction Reagent (Thermo Scientific, Cat# 87792) with 100× Protease and Phosphatase Inhibitor Cocktail (Cell Signaling, Cat# 5872) to a final 1× concentration, vortex thoroughly, and keep the buffer on ice. Prepare fresh for each experiment.

steps.title: Prepare SDS running buffer
steps.instruction: Add 100 mL 20× NuPAGE MES SDS Running Buffer (Thermo Fisher, Cat# NP0002) to 1900 mL Milli‑Q water, stir with a magnetic bar until uniform, and store the 1× running buffer at 20–25 °C (use within 1–2 days).

steps.title: Prepare transfer buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 100 mL 20× NuPAGE Transfer Buffer (Thermo Fisher, Cat# NP00061) with 1500 mL Milli‑Q water and 400 mL methanol (Thermo Fisher, Cat# A4524), stir extensively, and store the 1× buffer at 4 °C (use within 1–2 days).

steps.title: Prepare PBS/sucrose buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1.64 g sucrose (Sigma, Cat# S7903) in 36 mL Milli‑Q water, vortex until fully dissolved, add 4 mL 10× PBS (Corning, Cat# 46‑013CM), vortex again, and store at room temperature for up to 4 weeks.

steps.title: Prepare fixation buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1.64 g sucrose (Sigma, Cat# S7903) in 26 mL Milli‑Q water, vortex until clear, add 10 mL 16 % paraformaldehyde stock (Electron Microscopy Sciences, Cat# 15710‑S) and 4 mL 10× PBS, vortex, and store at 20–25 °C for up to 4 weeks.

steps.title: Prepare extraction buffer
steps.instruction: Add 4 mL 10× PBS to a 50 mL Falcon tube, add 35 mL Milli‑Q water, then add 1 mL 10 % Triton X‑100 stock (Sigma, Cat# T8787), vortex, and store at 20–25 °C for up to 4 weeks.

steps.title: Prepare blocking buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.44 g BSA (Sigma, Cat# A8806) in 34 mL Milli‑Q water, vortex until homogeneous, add 4 mL 10× PBS, then add 2 mL FBS (Gibco, Cat# A5256701), vortex, and store at 20–25 °C for up to 4 weeks.

steps.title: Make 1 mg/mL PEI Max stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1 g PEI Max (Polysciences, Cat# 24765‑1) in 900 mL Milli‑Q water, heat to 80 °C for 30–60 min with occasional stirring until clear, cool to 20–25 °C, adjust the final volume to 1 L, set pH to 7.0 with 1 N HCl or 1 N NaOH, filter through a 0.22 µm sterile filter, aliquot into sterile 15 or 50 mL tubes, store aliquots at –20 °C long‑term (short‑term up to 2 months at 4 °C). Note that the solution may appear cloudy initially but should become clear.

steps.title: Prepare 2 M Tris‑HCl pH 9.5 buffer
steps.instruction: Weigh 24.2 g Tris‑aminomethane (Sigma, Cat# T1503), add to ~80 mL Milli‑Q water, stir until dissolved, adjust pH to 9.5 with concentrated HCl, bring the volume to 100 mL with Milli‑Q water, filter‑sterilize (0.22 µm), and store at 20–25 °C short‑term or 4 °C for up to 2 weeks.

steps.title: Extract genomic DNA from neurons
steps.instruction: Wash 300 000 cultured hippocampal neurons (DIV 17‑21) infected with scrambled control or α‑syn CRISPR‑KO lentivirus with 1 mL 1× PBS, add 50 µL Lucigen QuickExtract DNA Extraction Solution (Biosearch Technologies, Cat# QE09050), pipette up/down gently, transfer to PCR tubes, incubate 68 °C for 15 min then 95 °C for 10 min, and store lysates at –20 °C.

steps.title: Identify potential off‑target sites
steps.instruction: Run CasOFFinder (http://www.rgenome.net/cas‑offinder/) using the guide RNA sequence, select the appropriate reference genome (mm10), set PAM for your CRISPR system, and use the following query parameters: Mismatch Number = 3, DNA Bulge Size = 0, RNA Bulge Size = 0. Record off‑target sites with ≤3 mismatches.

steps.title: Design primers for on/off‑targets
steps.instruction: Using SnapGene, design primers with 40‑60 % GC, length 18‑24 bp, starting/ending with C or G when possible, and melting temperatures matched. Target amplicon size 1000‑1500 bp; sequencing primers should lie 170‑300 bp upstream of the CRISPR cut site in the gRNA direction. Submit primer sequences to IDT for synthesis. Verify specificity with BLAT (https://genome.ucsc.edu/cgibin/hgBlat), perform in‑silico PCR (https://genome.ucsc.edu/cgi‑bin/hgPcr), and assess primer‑dimer formation with the Primer Analyzer tool (Thermo Fisher).

steps.title: Amplify genomic DNA by PCR
steps.instruction: Set up 50 µL PCR reactions with high‑fidelity polymerase (Q5 or Phusion): 0.5 µM each primer, 1 µL polymerase, and 100 ng gDNA per reaction. Include negative control (non‑transduced neurons) and scrambled sgRNA control. Perform 35 cycles (denaturation, annealing, extension per manufacturer’s protocol). After PCR, load 4 µL of product mixed with 1 µL 6× loading dye on a 1 % agarose gel to verify the expected band and absence of non‑specific bands. If non‑specific bands appear, increase annealing temperature or redesign primers, then repeat PCR.

substeps.instruction: Prepare master mix (excluding polymerase and primers).
Run 4 µL product + loading dye on 1 % agarose gel.
Assess band specificity; optimize if needed.

steps.title: Purify PCR products
steps.instruction: Purify amplified DNA using the QIAGEN QIAquick PCR Purification Kit (Cat# 28104) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Elute the purified DNA in 20‑30 µL molecular‑grade water. If non‑specific bands persist, excise the correct band from a gel, gel‑purify, dry thoroughly to remove ethanol, and re‑elute.

substeps.instruction: Apply PCR mix to QIAquick column.
If needed, gel‑purify the correct band.

steps.title: Submit samples for Sanger sequencing
steps.instruction: Send the purified PCR products to Genewiz (Azenta Life Sciences) for Sanger sequencing using the previously designed sequencing primers.

steps.title: Inspect control chromatograms
steps.instruction: Open the .ab1 files from negative control samples (untransduced or scrambled‑treated) in SnapGene or Benchling. Verify that traces show clean, single peaks with no insertions, deletions, or ambiguous bases before proceeding with edited samples.

steps.title: Perform TIDE analysis
steps.instruction: Upload the .ab1 files to the TIDE Batch tool (http://shinyapps.datacurators.nl/tide‑batch/) and run with default settings. Analyze both on‑target and off‑target sites (using the mismatching guide RNAs identified by CasOFFinder) to quantify insertion/deletion frequencies.
